description: API docs page, links, the milestone e2e and the written docs (plan.md items 13-17). A pure view-model builder turns the generated OpenAPI document into tags/operations/fields; /docs/api renders it (Paraglide strings, landmarks, headings, tables, code blocks, light/dark via tokens). The site gets a footer link and the org admin API keys tab links to it. e2e/api.e2e.ts proves 'create → start → report via key' plus the negative cases and that the UI reflects API changes. docs/PLAN.md marks M7 ✅ with implementation notes; README gets a REST API section. Ends with the full verification run. Depends on FEAT-001 and FEAT-002.

docs/PLAN.md: milestones table row `M7` -> `M7 ✅` (prettier realigns); Stack bullet 'generates the OpenAPI spec (`zod-openapi`)' -> '(`z.toJSONSchema`)'; architecture tree: auth/ comment adds requireApiKey, api/ comment 'endpoint definitions, error envelope, zod schemas -> OpenAPI', routes list adds `docs/api`; data model bullet `match_messages` (matchId, authorId or apiKeyName, asOrganizer, body, createdAt). Add `## Implementation notes (M7)` after the M6 notes, terse like M4–M6: (1) Each operation is defined once in `api/endpoints.ts` (method, path, tag, Zod schemas for params/query/body/response); routes wrap handlers in `endpoint()`, which checks the key, validates with those schemas and answers errors with the envelope, and the OpenAPI document is built from the same list; a db test matches every route file to a definition. (2) The spec uses Zod 4's `z.toJSONSchema` (OpenAPI 3.1 is JSON Schema 2020-12) with a small builder instead of `zod-openapi`; named schemas are registered in one registry and become `components.schemas`. (3) Keys: `Authorization: Bearer tm_<prefix>_<secret>`, looked up by prefix and compared by hash in constant time; `lastUsedAt` is written at most once a minute. A key only sees its organization: other organizations' tournaments are 404 like missing ones. No CORS, since keys belong on servers. Rate limiting is still open. (4) Errors are `{ error: { code, message, issues? } }`: Zod 400 with issues, keys 401, unknown or other-org resources 404, `ServiceError.kind` conflict 409 / invalid 422 / not_found 404; unknown routes and methods use it too. Send JSON: SvelteKit's CSRF check rejects form content types from other origins before the API runs. (5) Results set with a key are `api_key` reports through the organizer override; `POST …/reports` reports for a participant with the players' rules. Key messages are organizer messages labelled with the key's name, copied to `match_messages.api_key_name` so revoking the key keeps the label. (6) The API deletes drafts only; the admin page still deletes anything after typing the address. (7) `/docs/api` renders the generated document, linked from the footer and the API keys tab.

README.md: after '## Bracket themes' add '## REST API': organizations can run their tournaments over a REST API at `/api/v1`, e.g. from a Discord bot; create a key in the organization admin on the **API keys** tab (it's shown once) and send it as `Authorization: Bearer tm_<prefix>_<secret>` with a ```bash curl -H "Authorization: Bearer tm_…" http://localhost:5173/api/v1/tournaments ``` example; a key only sees its own organization; bodies are JSON; the OpenAPI 3.1 document is at `/api/v1/openapi.json` and `/docs/api` shows it as a reference.

One finding and deviation: SvelteKit 3's CSRF check (csrf.js is_csrf_forbidden) returns a plain-text 403 'Cross-site POST form submissions are forbidden' for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE with NO content type (not only form types) when the Origin doesn't match, so body-less calls (open-registration, start, DELETE) need `Content-Type: application/json`. The e2e `auth()` helper sends it on every request; the docs page text (api_docs_auth_header), the OpenAPI info.description (one-line edit in openapi.ts), README and the PLAN.md M7 note say so. Verification on the final tree: format clean; check 0 errors / 0 warnings; lint clean (prettier + eslint); test:unit --run 29 files / 332 tests pass (FEAT-002's 319 + 13 in reference.spec.ts); test:e2e e2e/api.e2e.ts 2 passed; full test:e2e 11 passed (9 existing + 2 new). Integration (fix loop, iteration 1, no verdict.json yet): reviewed the seams between FEAT-001/002/003 against plan.md and the brief's done-when list. Every admin UI action (general update/delete/lifecycle; theme; structure; requirements; participants add/remove/up/down/check-in/shuffle, with up/down covered by setSeeds; matches result/clear/clearHelp; room override/clear/clearHelp/message) has a REST equivalent that calls the same service. The 21 endpoint routes only call guards, services and serializers. Every ChatMessage consumer (MatchChat, toMessage, specs) handles `author: null`. The docs page uses only tokens defined in light and dark, and the footer doesn't affect the bracket canvas, whose height is capped at 75vh. No code changes were needed. Verification in one shell call on the final tree: `corepack pnpm format` (no changes); `corepack pnpm check` 0 errors / 0 warnings; `corepack pnpm lint` clean (prettier + eslint); `corepack pnpm test:unit --run` 29 files / 332 tests passed; `$env:PATH = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\corepack-shims;$env:PATH"; corepack pnpm test:e2e` 11 passed (9 existing + 2 in e2e/api.e2e.ts). Open item for the reviewer, documented rather than changed: in production builds only (respond.js skips it in dev), SvelteKit 3 answers POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE that have no content type or a form content type and no matching Origin with its own plain-text 403 before the API runs. That 403 is not the envelope. The docs page, OpenAPI info.description, README and the PLAN.md M7 note tell clients to send Content-Type: application/json. The only way around it is to turn off kit's csrf checkOrigin and reimplement the check for non-API routes in hooks. That is a security change, so it is left to the user.
